correctness.rationale: Parseval applied to P^4 for normalized Haar measure yields the sum of squared fourth-convolution coefficients. Taking coefficient magnitudes individually can only increase the sum. For positive magnitudes, the z^3 coefficient has the two nonzero contributions 4ab^3 and 4a^3c, so equality requires the asserted phase congruence. Any collision of multinomial exponents differs by an integer multiple of (2,−3,1), so this condition also aligns all other collisions. The degree-eight difference 9221771(a²+b²+c²)^4−10^6 M needs only be checked on the positive barycentric simplex by homogeneity, with the origin automatic. The four exact scaled linear substitutions cover each parent simplex; nonnegative leaf coefficients therefore give a valid bound on the whole octant. An independent exact-integer replay constructed M from fourth convolution and reproduced 18 monomials, 81 total nodes, 61 certified leaves and depth 13; it also independently checked the strict lower witness inequality at (576602,605492,548552). Compactness of the energy-one sphere gives a maximizer. With at most two terms, the fourth-power frequency indices are distinct and the ratio is 1+12s+6s² with s the product of the two energy fractions, 0≤s≤1/4. It is at most 70/16, strictly below the witness. Thus every maximizer has three nonzero terms and, since its magnitude-matched phase-aligned counterpart cannot improve it, the stated phase condition holds for every maximizer.
